newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal and soyoil end lower on weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal and soyoil end lower on weather.

text.p: CBOT soymeal and soyoil futures ended lower on Thursday, taking cues from soybeans, on perceptions of ideal weather and on position squaring ahead of Friday's USDA supply and demand report, traders said.

Bull spreading was a key feature, tied to expectations USDA would leave old crop ending stocks unchanged at 130 million bushels but would increase new crop projections from last month's 240 million bushels.
Traders said increased acreage and good growing weather would likely lead to a bumper crop, leaving larger marketing year ending supplies.

Wednesday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook called for above normal rain and below normal temperatures in the Midwest from July 15 to 19. Those conditions were deemed conducive to crop development.

Losses were limited by USDA export sales data which came in above trade expectations. USDA Thursday put net sales of old crop soymeal in the week ended July 3 at 92,300 tonnes, above expectations for 20,000 to 30,000 tonnes.
Soymeal ended $4.10 per ton lower to unchanged with August steady at $243.80. Soyoil was down 0.36 to 0.22 cent per lb with August down 0.30 at 21.89.

On the day, commercials were again buyers of both soyoil and soymeal. Trade sources said Produce Grain bought August and sold September. ADM, Cargill and Central Soya were also said to be buyers of the nearby.
"Cash meal seems to be tightening up," one cash-connected trader said. "I wouldn't be surprised to see crush pick back up here in the next few weeks."

In soyoil, ADM, Produce Grain, Cargill and Continental Grain were all among the buyers while LIT was the primary seller. Traders said LIT sold 600 lots August, 500 September, 200 December and 100 October.
Bull spreads were active in soymeal. ADM spread 400 lots September/December at $26.00, premium September.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 21,000 lots, down from the 30,257 lots traded Wednesday. Soyoil volume was pegged at 17,000 lots, against Wednesday's 28,893.
